scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

problem_definition_history.requested_solution: SH-CS requests an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and automatically fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills (CL-01).
symptoms: Dispute ticket volume rose from ~600/month (Jun-Jul: 610, 590) to ~1220/month (Aug-Sep: 1180, 1260), roughly doubling (E-04).
59% (1785/3025) of disputed bills are tagged ACTUAL read type versus 41% ESTIMATED (E-01).
Manual-read route completion fell to 88% against a 95% target in Aug-Sep across 9200 accounts (E-03).
Dispute response times remain within the 3.0-day SLA: median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days across 2440 tickets (E-07).
problem_definition_history.root_problem: Dispute tickets doubled Aug-Sep (E-04) not because responses are slow (within SLA, E-07) or tariffs changed (none logged, E-02); 59% of disputed bills are ACTUAL-read, not estimate-substituted (E-01), pointing to a defect in the billing import/validation step that processes actual reads (candidate: an import-validation rule change, H-RULE-CHANGE-DEFECT) as the primary mechanism producing incorrect bills and driving the surge.

challenges.rationale: ER-1: premise E-01 revised by E-12: re-read under E-12 (accepted premise check) — PR-CHAIN-5: E-12 shows 95.5% (1184/1240) of ESTIMATED-tagged disputed bills had an AMI read delivered and exported but rejected at import for high consumption, versus only 4.5% (56) with no read received at all; the premise's attributed mechanism (route-completion/field-read shortfall) explains only the small minority, so the stated cause of the ESTIMATED bucket's estimate-substitution is wrong and the chain's division of labor between buckets must be redefined.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

H-WRONG-BILLS-AI-FIX.statement: Dispute surge is caused by incorrect bills from an unspecified defect, and the correct remedy is an AI agent that both auto-answers tickets and automatically corrects the bills.

H-RULE-CHANGE-DEFECT.statement: A change to billing import validation rules around August introduced a systematic defect (e.g., misclassifying read types or estimate substitution) that is producing incorrect bills.

H-AMI-EXPORT-FAILURE.statement: The nightly MDMS AMI read export (H-MDMS-BILL) began failing or delivering incomplete reads since August, causing fallback to estimates and wrong bills.

H-FIELD-READ-HANDOFF-FAILURE.statement: The daily manual-read upload from MeterWorks (H-FIELD-BILL) started failing, being late, or being incomplete since August, forcing estimate substitution and wrong bills.

H-CS-CATEGORIZATION-ARTIFACT.statement: Underlying bill accuracy did not change; the apparent doubling of dispute tickets since August reflects a change in CRM ticket tagging/categorization or SLA tracking, not more wrong bills.

H-FIELD-STAFFING-SHORTAGE.statement: A contract headcount shortfall at MeterWorks since August reduced completed manual read routes, driving estimate substitution and wrong bills.

H-ACTUAL-READ-BILLING-DEFECT.statement: Since the majority of disputed bills (1785 of 3025) are associated with ACTUAL reads rather than estimates, a defect in billing/tariff processing of actual reads (not estimate substitution) may be a primary driver of the dispute surge.

H-HIGH-CONSUMPTION-REJECT-RULE.statement: A billing import validation rule rejects AMI reads flagged as high consumption (billing_import_status=REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION), causing fallback to an estimated bill for the large majority of ESTIMATED-read disputes.

H-BV17-UNIT-SCALING-DEFECT.statement: BV-17 (deployed 2026-08-01) compares the raw AMI register value directly against 12-month m3 consumption history with no unit scaling, which could cause legitimate reads to be misclassified as high-consumption and rejected at import, generating the estimate-substitution surge.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Of 3025 disputed bills, 1240 (41%) are tagged ESTIMATED read type and 1785 (59%) are tagged ACTUAL read type, so a majority of disputes attach to bills built from ACTUAL (not estimated) reads.

re-read under E-12 (accepted premise check) — PR-CHAIN-5: E-12 shows 95.5% (1184/1240) of ESTIMATED-tagged disputed bills had an AMI read delivered and exported but rejected at import for high consumption, versus only 4.5% (56) with no read received at all; the premise's attributed mechanism (route-completion/field-read shortfall) explains only the small minority, so the stated cause of the ESTIMATED bucket's estimate-substitution is wrong and the chain's division of labor between buckets must be redefined.

billing-db's tariff_change_log contains zero records, meaning no tariff rate/structure changes were logged in the period covered — there is no recorded tariff-rate-change event that could explain the August dispute surge via a tariff edit.

Field manual-read route completion for the Aug–Sep period was 88% against a 95% target (9200 manual-read accounts), confirming a real but modest shortfall in completed manual reads during the dispute surge window. A ~7-point completion gap could drive some estimate substitution, but is unlikely by itself to account for the roughly doubled dispute volume.

CRM monthly dispute counts show ~600/month in Jun-Jul (610, 590) rising to ~1200/month in Aug-Sep (1180, 1260), roughly doubling. This confirms the ticket-volume increase itself is real and coincides with the reported surge window, but the record contains only counts by month and says nothing about ticket cause, categorization, or bill accuracy.

E-05.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL (Billing Operations Lead) claims no tariff change occurred this year. This is a non-authoritative, unverified stakeholder claim that happens to agree with the authoritative tariff_change_log record (E-02, 0 records), but adds no new evidentiary weight beyond that tool record.

E-06.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD claims MeterWorks has been short three readers since July, causing routes to run late and those customers' bills to be estimated. This is an unverified claim from a stakeholder incentivized toward a headcount-increase narrative, offering a candidate mechanistic explanation for the modest route-completion shortfall already seen in E-03, not new authoritative evidence.

crm-tickets.dispute_response_times (E-07) reports median 1.6 days and p90 2.8 days against a 3.0-day SLA across 2440 tickets, meaning dispute tickets are currently being resolved within the response-time SLA on average and even at the 90th percentile. This undercuts the premise that tickets are going unanswered or answered too slowly, which was the stated rationale for an auto-answering AI agent.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: E-08 is a service-contract document stating the utility may request route priority changes but these are executed only after Field Operations Manager confirmation; this corroborates (does not alter) the existing K-DISPATCH human-approval requirement for push_route_update, and does not speak to the cause of the dispute surge.

interpretation_history.interpretation: billing-db.accounts_estimated_last_cycle (E-09) returns only 320 accounts across 40 routes with fields account_id and route — it carries no read_type, tariff, import-status, or dispute-linkage fields, so despite being authoritative/complete it cannot by itself audit the ACTUAL-read disputed-bill defect that work item W-WI-AUDIT-ACTUAL-READ-BILLS intended it for; it only tells us how many accounts were on an estimated (not actual) read last cycle and how many routes they span.

interpretation_history.interpretation: route-log.lagging_routes (E-10) identifies 14 specific routes with below-target completion (sample: route R-00 at 0.70), giving route-level granularity behind the aggregate 88% completion figure (E-03) and showing which routes drive that shortfall, relevant to the pending field-handoff verification work item (W-WI-VERIFY-FIELD-HANDOFF).

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-AMI reports that MDMS export access for Lakeside was provisioned today under vendor ticket TX-4471; this is an unverified stakeholder claim that the blocker behind U-MDMS-ACCESS-PENDING / the ACCESS_PENDING state on mdms-export:read_events_for_disputed_estimated may now be resolved, but mdms-export tool_health is still recorded DEGRADED and no tool record yet confirms the access actually works.

For the 1240 disputed bills tagged ESTIMATED read type (E-01), E-12 shows 1184 (95.5%) had an AMI read delivered before cutoff and exported to billing but rejected at import with status REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, while only 56 (4.5%) genuinely had no read received at all. This points to a billing-import validation rule rejecting high-consumption AMI reads as the dominant cause of estimate substitution, not AMI export failure or field-read non-delivery.

E-13.content: billing-config.validation_rule_changes → 2 record(s): {"change": "high-consumption check compares raw register value with 12-month m3 history", "deployed": "2026-08-01", "rule": "BV-17", "unit_scaling": "none"}; {"change": "label text", "deployed": "2026-03-02", "rule": "BV-09"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: E-13 (billing-config.validation_rule_changes) shows rule BV-17 was deployed on 2026-08-01, changing the high-consumption import check to compare the raw AMI register value directly with 12-month m3 history, with no unit scaling applied; the only other change, BV-09, was a cosmetic label-text edit on 2026-03-02. BV-17's deployment date coincides exactly with the start of the dispute surge and matches the REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION mechanism already seen in E-12, confirming a real billing-import rule change occurred and giving it a concrete, specific defect candidate (missing unit scaling in a raw-value comparison).

E-14 shows AMI firmware v4.2 (rolled out 2026-06) reports register values in units of "0.1 m3" while firmware v3.x reports in plain "m3". Since BV-17 (E-13) compares raw register values directly to 12-month m3 history with no unit scaling, v4.2 raw readings would read ~10x higher than true m3 consumption — matching that all 1184 REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION bills in E-12 are tagged firmware "v4.2".

U-RULE-CHANGE-OCCURRED.question: Did billing import validation rules actually change around August, and if so what changed?
U-RULE-CHANGE-OCCURRED.decision_impact: Confirms or refutes the primary causal mechanism (H-RULE-CHANGE-DEFECT); if no rule change occurred, the root-cause narrative must shift to another defect source before any remediation is proposed.
U-RULE-CHANGE-OCCURRED.resolution_path: Query billing-config rule change log (DA-RULES) for Jul-Aug entries and cross-reference the timing against the dispute surge onset (E-04).
U-RULE-CHANGE-OCCURRED.safe_placeholder: Proceed with the diagnostic audit of disputed ACTUAL-read bills (DA-BILL) without assuming a confirmed rule-change defect; take no bill-correcting action until the rule-log query completes.
U-RULE-CHANGE-OCCURRED.resolution: Yes — rule BV-17 was deployed 2026-08-01, changing the high-consumption check to compare raw register value against 12-month m3 history with no unit scaling; BV-09 (2026-03-02) was only a cosmetic label-text change and unrelated.

U-MDMS-ACCESS-PENDING.question: Will Telemetrix provision the pending MDMS export access needed to check AMI read events behind the ESTIMATED-read disputes?
U-MDMS-ACCESS-PENDING.decision_impact: Without MDMS data, the minority ESTIMATED-read dispute bucket (41%) cannot be cross-checked against AMI read events, limiting the ability to rule out an AMI-side contribution for that bucket.
U-MDMS-ACCESS-PENDING.resolution_path: Continue the pending vendor access request noted in the ACCESS_PENDING recovery decision and re-poll mdms-export tool health.
U-MDMS-ACCESS-PENDING.safe_placeholder: Proceed with the billing-db/route-log based diagnosis of the majority ACTUAL-read bucket; defer the AMI-event cross-check until access is granted.
U-MDMS-ACCESS-PENDING.resolution: mdms-export returned an authoritative, complete record set (E-12) via read_events_for_disputed_estimated, confirming the vendor-provisioned export access now functions and resolving the access-pending blocker.

U-TICKET-CATEGORIZATION-CHANGE.question: Did CRM dispute-ticket tagging/categorization or SLA tracking change in August, inflating the apparent ticket count without a change in underlying bill accuracy?
U-TICKET-CATEGORIZATION-CHANGE.decision_impact: If categorization changed, the doubling in E-04 may be partly a measurement artifact rather than more wrong bills, which would invalidate A-CRM-COUNT-INTEGRITY and the dispute-volume success criterion.
U-TICKET-CATEGORIZATION-CHANGE.resolution_path: Review crm-tickets categorization/config change history for August and compare ticket definitions before and after.
U-TICKET-CATEGORIZATION-CHANGE.safe_placeholder: Report M-DISPUTE-VOLUME alongside the read-type-based share metric and flag it as provisional until categorization stability is confirmed.

U-FIELD-STAFFING-CONTRIBUTION.question: To what extent does the confirmed route-completion shortfall (88% vs 95%) and the claimed reader staffing shortage explain the minority ESTIMATED-read dispute bucket?
U-FIELD-STAFFING-CONTRIBUTION.decision_impact: Determines whether any route/dispatch remediation (push_route_update) is warranted or whether the shortfall is incidental to the dominant ACTUAL-read defect.
U-FIELD-STAFFING-CONTRIBUTION.resolution_path: Correlate route-log completion shortfall records with ESTIMATED-tagged disputed bill accounts and SH-FIELD's staffing claim (E-06).
U-FIELD-STAFFING-CONTRIBUTION.safe_placeholder: Do not execute push_route_update until the route-completion contribution to disputes is quantified; any route change stays gated behind SH-FIELD runtime confirmation per K-DISPATCH.
U-FIELD-STAFFING-CONTRIBUTION.resolution: E-12 shows only 56 of 1240 (4.5%) ESTIMATED-read disputes involve a genuinely missing read; staffing/route-completion shortfall can at most explain that small minority, with the remaining 95.5% caused by billing-import rejection of delivered reads.

U-ACTUAL-READ-DEFECT-MECHANISM.question: What mechanism produces incorrect bills for the 59% of disputed bills (1785 of 3025) tagged ACTUAL read type (E-01) — is it the same BV-17/firmware v4.2 unit-mismatch defect affecting accepted (non-rejected) reads, or a distinct cause?
U-ACTUAL-READ-DEFECT-MECHANISM.decision_impact: Determines whether the BV-17 unit-scaling fix alone resolves the dispute surge or whether a separate remedy is needed for the majority of dispute volume.
U-ACTUAL-READ-DEFECT-MECHANISM.resolution_path: Run audit_actual_read_disputed_bills against billing-db on a sample of ACTUAL-read disputed bills, checking firmware and import-status fields analogous to E-12's method.
U-ACTUAL-READ-DEFECT-MECHANISM.safe_placeholder: Treat the BV-17/firmware fix as resolving only the confirmed ESTIMATED/REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION bucket (1184 of 3025 disputes); do not claim the ACTUAL-read majority is resolved until audited.

A-READ-TYPE-TAG-RELIABLE.statement: The ESTIMATED/ACTUAL read_type tag recorded in billing-db reliably identifies which process path produced each disputed bill, not a data-entry artifact.

A-CRM-COUNT-INTEGRITY.statement: The CRM monthly dispute counts (E-04) measure a stable ticket-categorization scheme, so the doubling reflects more real disputes rather than a change in what counts as a dispute.

A-TARIFF-LOG-COMPLETE.statement: billing-db's tariff_change_log is a complete record of all tariff rate/structure changes, so its zero count genuinely rules out tariff edits as a cause.

A-BV17-CAUSAL-MECHANISM.statement: The numeric mismatch between BV-17's unscaled raw-value comparison and firmware v4.2's 0.1 m3 register unit is the actual causal trigger of REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, not an unobserved confound merely correlated with the v4.2 rollout timing.

problem_definition.requested_solution: SH-CS requests an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and automatically fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills (CL-01).
symptoms: Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul: 610, 590) to ~1220/month (Aug-Sep: 1180, 1260) (E-04).

Of 1240 disputed bills tagged ESTIMATED read type, 1184 (95.5%) had a valid AMI read delivered and exported but were rejected at billing import with status REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, versus only 56 (4.5%) with no read received at all (E-12).
Billing-config rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01, compares raw AMI register values directly against 12-month m3 history with no unit scaling (E-13), coinciding with the surge start date.

AMI firmware v4.2 (rollout 2026-06) reports register values in 0.1 m3 units rather than plain m3, unlike firmware v3.x (E-14); all 1184 REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION bills are tagged firmware v4.2 (E-12).
59% (1785/3025) of disputed bills are tagged ACTUAL read type (E-01); the mechanism behind this majority bucket is not yet explained by the BV-17/firmware finding.
Dispute response times remain within the 3.0-day SLA (median 1.6d, p90 2.8d, 2440 tickets) (E-07), ruling out slow ticket handling as the cause.
No tariff rate/structure changes are logged this year (0 records in billing-db tariff_change_log) (E-02), ruling out a tariff edit as the cause.

proposal.summary: SH-CS initially asked for an AI agent to auto-answer dispute tickets and auto-fix wrong bills after tickets roughly doubled since August (CL-01, E-04). Investigation first framed the problem as actual-read bills being wrong (PD-1@v1), but that premise was invalidated by E-12, and the problem was redefined (PD-1@v2): 95.5% (1184/1240) of ESTIMATED-tagged disputed bills had a valid AMI read that was rejected at import as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION (E-12), because rule BV-17 deployed 2026-08-01 compares raw AMI register values to 12-month m3 history with no unit scaling (E-13), while firmware v4.2 reports in 0.1 m3 units (E-14), causing legitimate v4.2 reads to look ~10x too high and get rejected, triggering an estimate the customer disputes. Slow response times (E-07) and tariff changes (E-02) were ruled out as causes. The release delivers this confirmed root-cause finding (query_billing_rule_change_log:DA-RULES) rather than the originally requested auto-fixing agent, because automated bill writes are prohibited (K-BILLWRITE) and the broader fix requires ORG-UTIL/Billing Operations action outside this agent's scope; the decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION with several verification items left open rather than fully resolved.
key_points: Original request: build an AI agent to auto-answer tickets and fix wrong bills, triggered by doubled dispute volume (CL-01, E-04).
The first problem framing (PD-1@v1, actual-read bills defective) was invalidated by E-12 and superseded by PD-1@v2.

Root cause confirmed: BV-17 rule (deployed 2026-08-01, E-13) lacks unit scaling and firmware v4.2 reports in 0.1 m3 (E-14), causing legitimate high reads to be rejected (REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION) for 1184 of 1240 ESTIMATED-tagged disputed bills (E-12).
Slow ticket response (E-07) and tariff changes (E-02) were checked and ruled out as drivers of the surge.

The requested 'AI agent that automatically fixes wrong bills' was rejected (H-WRONG-BILLS-AI-FIX status REJECTED) because no automated bill writes are permitted (K-BILLWRITE); any fix/reprocessing must go through Billing Operations.

DEFINE Gate returned CONDITIONAL_PASS and the release carries open verification obligations (VOB-R-5, VOB-U-ACTUAL-READ-DEFECT-MECHANISM, VOB-U-TICKET-CATEGORIZATION-CHANGE), which is why the decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION rather than an unconditional release.

Release scope delivered is limited to the confirmed billing-rule-change-log finding (query_billing_rule_change_log:DA-RULES per SD-2); the larger ACTUAL-read bucket (59% of disputed bills, E-01) and ticket-categorization question remain unaddressed in this release.
